items.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.content:
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.

The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago, when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park, owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.

The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy, but later allowed to go ahead.

Otherwise, such exports are very rare, say experts. David Newton, programme office director for east and southern Africa for Traffic, an NGO that monitors the trade in wild animals and plants, said: “It is very unusual to see baobabs being used as ornamental plants … mainly because they are exceptionally difficult to dig out of the ground and transport, and then to successfully re-establish.”

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, who has led efforts to replant the South African trees, said she believes they have a good chance of surviving if they are replanted quickly. The winter months of May to October, when the trees lose their leaves and are dormant, is a good time to move them.

“As soon as spring starts \[in November\], the trees use their water to flush their new leaves, and that’s when we need to get them into the ground as soon as possible,” she said.

The rescue mission has faced delays because of the challenges associated with moving such large trees, which are transported on special trucks capable of carrying abnormal loads. The five baobabs weigh between 19 and 29 tonnes, have a diameter of up to 4.5 metres (15ft) and a height of up to 12.5 metres.

Baobabs, known as the tree of life, are protected under South African law, which means a permit is required to cut or disturb them.

“A baobab isn’t just part of an ecosystem, it is an ecosystem in itself,” said Wambui Ippolito, a landscape designer, lecturer and horticulturist from Kenya. “These trees are biodiversity anchors.”

Animals ranging from bats and bush babies, to grey-headed parrots and the southern ground hornbill shelter in its cavities, while elephants, monkeys and warthogs feast on its fruit.

The trees have huge cultural importance, added Ippolito. “It has always been a sacred tree in Africa. It doesn’t matter where you go: Senegal, Mali, Ghana – wherever you go, if there is a community around a baobab tree, that tree is sacred,” she said. “Somebody’s great-great-great-great-great-grandparents sat under that tree, and it is part of human history in that area.”

Baobabs have shallow roots, which means they do not need to be planted very deeply, and these regrow fairly quickly, said Venter. Once replanted, the trees will be stabilised with cables and protected by electric fences to prevent damage from elephants.

The trees are thought to be between 200 and 300 years old. “Baobabs easily reach 1,000 years old, so they’ve got a few hundred years ahead of them if they survive,” said Venter.

A criminal case has been opened against the owner of a landscaping company allegedly responsible for the illegal harvesting and transportation of the trees.

*Find more age of extinction coverage here, and follow the biodiversity reporters Rebecca Ratcliffe, Phoebe Weston and Patrick Greenfield in the Guardian app for more nature coverage.*

items.title: 田渊栋创业合伙人：通往 AGI 最快的路，只能是 AI 造 AI | CoRL 2026
items.content:
Recursive 联创 Jeff Clune ：“QD、开放式、AI 生成算法，我觉得它们就是下一代伟大的 AI。”

    作者丨邓哲敏

    编辑丨齐铖湧

11 月 12 日，CoRL 2026 最后一天。主会已经结束，32 场 Workshop 密集进行，其中一场聚焦持续自进化（Continually Self-Improving），英属哥伦比亚大学教授、Uber AI Labs 创始成员 Jeff Clune 受邀来做分享。

今年 5 月，田渊栋（前 Meta FAIR 研究总监、ELF OpenGo 主导者）与其他七位联合创始人创办 Recursive Superintelligence，Jeff Clune 是其中一位。这家公司首轮融资 6.5 亿美元，投后估值 46.5 亿美元，谷歌 GV 与 Greycroft 联合领投，英伟达和 AMD 两大算力巨头同时押注。

大多数打着递归式自我改进（RSI）旗号的团队做的是后训练层面的代码自改写、prompt 自优化、agent 工作流自搜索，而 **Recursive 是全球唯一在预训练阶段做 RSI 的公司**。田渊栋近期透露，他们的系统已经能自己写出高性能的 GPU Kernel——可以理解为显卡的底层计算程序，相当于直接跟硬件打交道的核心代码——在部分任务上比专业工程团队写得还好。

Jeff Clune 在自进化方面的研究，也从一开始就瞄准了最上游的模型训练环节。2019 年，他发表了一篇当时看来近乎科学幻想的论文，提出**通往 AGI 最快的路是人造出“能造 AI 的 AI”**，并命名为 AI 生成算法。路线图上有三根支柱：自己会进化的架构、自己会进化的学习算法、自动生成的训练环境。注意第三根柱子的措辞，“训练环境”，不是“推理环境”或“部署环境”。

六年过去，这张路线图正在被逐一兑现：能自己改写自己代码的达尔文哥德尔机，把 SWE-bench 从 20% 刷到了 50%；能自己出题、自己跑实验、自己写论文的 AI 科学家，投出去的稿件通过了同行评审。Jeff Clune 在演讲中更细致地梳理了自己的工作。

以下是AI科技评论（雷峰网）带来的现场演讲精编。

生活里有这样一个悖论：越是死磕难题，越容易失败；你先不管那个大目标，反而能走更远。

科学和技术史上，每一件极难的事，都有同样的性质。用火做饭的年代，你只想要做饭更快，就永远造不出微波炉。没有计算机的年代，你只资助算得更快的人，就永远得不到计算机。因为想要得到计算机，就需要有人搞电、搞真空管，这些技术根本不是奔着“算得更快”发明出来的。

所以解决难题唯一的办法，**是像基础科学家那样，去试试自己能做什么、能解什么**，然后在目标之间切换，**根据你觉得“有可能”和“有意思”的东西，去挑新的目标。**

“换目标”这个想法来自 2016 年的一篇论文。假如你是做机器人的，你想让机器人往前走，算法却开始学习爬行和单腿站立保持平衡，别把这些当成没用的小动作扔掉。它们虽然没有让机器人前进的速度明显变快，但可能是前进运动的垫脚石。我们希望算法能抓住这种“诶，这个有意思”的发现。

这就是创新引擎（innovation engines）的想法。自然的演化、文化的演化都是创新引擎，共用一套配方：存档里装着发明过的一切，把东西取出来，稍加修改和组合，如果变成了更好的版本，就把这个更好的放回存档里。

今天给你们讲三类算法，都在试着**复现这种创新的力量**：质量多样性（QD）算法、开放式算法、AI 生成算法。

**QD 不追求唯一最优解，而是满世界地问：这个问题，我到底能有哪些截然不同的好解法？**

最流行、也最有代表性的是 MAP-Elites，我十几年前做的。先挑几个在意的变异维度（比如身高），加一个性能指标（比如速度），然后拿一个参数向量描述机器人，评估出它的各项指标，放进多维存档里对应的格子。接着开始循环：取一个指标出来改一下，重新评估，如果它是这个格子里见过最好的，就换进去，一直重复。它给你的不是一个点，而是一整张曲面——哪里好、哪里差、哪里能做，全都看得见。

2015 年我们用 QD 做软体机器人。经典优化只能拿到低性能解，刻意鼓励多样性，反而多样性更少，因为系统找到了高性能解，却不愿拿性能换多样性。换成 QD，同样算力，探索覆盖完全不一样了。你还能在这些存档里“做科研”：把某个格子里最终最好的解往前回溯它的祖先，会发现搜索走了一条很绕的路。

2021 年我们又用 QD 解决强化学习里的硬探索问题：用最高质量到达尽可能多的状态。我们用这个去玩《蒙特祖玛的复仇》，直接把领域天花板掀了，超过人类世界纪录，还一路解掉了所有关卡，打赢了当时所有最好的探索方法。

不过 QD 再强，还是被困在单一环境里。这就引出开放式算法，我研究了一辈子的东西。我们想要一个**能永远创新下去的算法**，哪怕跑十亿年，你还是想回来看看，因为它还在创新。

谁能搞定这个，我觉得该给他发个大奖。据我所知，目前只有两个开放式算法：自然演化和文化演化。关键是，每解决一个问题，就打开了新问题，而不是朝某个基准的分数收敛。

几年前我们在 Uber AI Labs 做了 POET，第一次把环境本身也当成基因组的一部分，让环境存档不断生长，同时允许换目标。有意思的是，POET 发明并解决了很多很难的、各不相同的题目。

让我们退一步看看整个领域的野心：AGI、ASI、RSI，随你怎么叫。我在 2019 年一篇讲 AI 生成算法的论文里说过一个趋势：算力和数据越多，手工设计的流程和组件就越会被学出来的替代**。**把这个逻辑套到 AGI 身上，**通往 AGI 最快的路，就是能造出更好 AI 的 AI。我当时叫 AI 生成算法，现在大家叫递归式自我改进。**

要做成这事，**至少三根支柱要往前推：架构（Transformer 不会是最后一个）、学习算法、自动生成训练环境。**今天主要讲第三根柱子。

真正的开放式算法需要巨大的环境搜索空间，但绝大多数环境要么不可能、要么太难、要么太简单。怎么保证新环境跟过去“有意思地不同”？现在可以直接问基础模型：我做过这 12 个环境了，下一个有意思的技能是什么？这样就能绕开“怎么定义有意思”这个老大难。

光能提任务还不够，还得知道怎么自动给任何任务设计奖励、判断有没有解出来，这叫通用奖励函数。一条路是把任务视频喂给视频语言模型，另一条是让 GPT 现场写奖励代码。均匀采样、单一指标都走不通，但 OMNI 会慢慢学出一套聪明的课程。

不过我们还是被困在厨房里。想更有野心，就得进入“达尔文完备”（Darwin-complete）的搜索空间。

一个是代码，我们做了 OMNI-EPIC，让系统用代码生成任何环境，于是有了这些障碍赛道，也能生成逻辑题、编程题、清理餐厅的机器人，类型可以非常不同。

二是神经网络本身，这个项目叫 Genie，一个世界模型，我和 DeepMind 的同事一起做的。你给它文本、图像、草图，它就生成环境。第一代只有一秒、糊糊的二维视频；九个月后 Genie 2 有了三维世界；再八个月后 Genie 3 基本是 3A 游戏级渲染器，Waymo 拿它训练自动驾驶。想象一下 Genie 4、5、10 会有多强？

接下来看这套套路有多通用。第一是智能体系统的自动设计，以前是人手工搭复杂智能体工作流，那不如直接去搜索智能体系统，让 AI 造更好的 AI，结果是它们很快超过了当时所有手工设计的脚手架。第二，我们让一个性能高的智能体存档不断生长，它变好，而且经常先变差才能变好。再往前是 Hyperagents，让智能体能改自己的代码、也能改进自我提升的能力。同样的想法也用于持续学习，学会给任务记笔记，之后遇到类似任务当场取用。

最后是 AI 科学家，几个月前我们发在 Nature 上的文章讨论了一个问题：AI 能不能把写论文的全流程做完？答案是能。

它能生成想法、设计并跑实验、分析和可视化、写完稿件、自己给自己做同行评审。我们把它的一些论文拿去做同行评审，被接收了，而且在 workshop 里，评分比当年人类投稿里 45% 的都高。而且有 scaling 规律，模型越好，做得越好。所以，未来不会只是某篇论文，而是 AI 科学家不断读自己的发现，一个创新接一个创新。

这就是现在 AI 最热的题目之一：递归式自我改进。我和朋友成立了公司叫 Recursive，就是奔着开放式 AI 去的。图像生成的十年，从糟糕透顶到接近完美，我们现在大概就在中间那个位置，而递归式自我改进大概刚处在刚刚勉强能用的位置。

最后我想说，QD、开放式、AI 生成算法，这些东西会不断创造垫脚石、换目标、学会创新，很可能是通往超级智能最快的路。所以我鼓励你们在自己的研究领域里想想怎么用上这些想法，我觉得它们就是下一代伟大的 AI。

**▎Q：你的方法看起来是被环境的特征卡住的，这些特征的多样性、规模、评估的成本，你觉得该怎么解决？**

A：很多人已经在机器人上用了这些想法，我前面提到的那些项目就是。你也可以拿我们在 Nature 那篇论文里做的东西，学一个高质量任务库，再想办法把它利用起来做迁移。你可以在仿真里用海量的、多样的任务训练，拿到很多技能；去真实世界里试；然后额外做一个小算法，去只在迁移得好的那些东西上训练。

以上为现场精炼干货版，演讲实录全文，可添加下方作者联系方式。

**国际机器人顶会 CoRL 2026 已经召开，欢迎参会的研究者、学生，以及关注 AI 前沿进展的读者加入我们雷峰网的交流群。**

在这里，你可以认识同行、交流研究，分享**招生信息、科研合作、约饭、投稿、组队参会**等，寻找潜在的合作伙伴。

大会期间，我们也会持续带来**现场报道速递、嘉宾演讲解读、前沿方向梳理和论坛精华**。

**会场见，也在群里见。**

**? 进群传送门：** 扫码进群或添加微信szhsn610，备注：CoRL+单位/学校+姓名+方向。

items.title: Google 杀入 Jev 核心赛道：Gemini Decision 1 五项基准领先两项落后
items.content:
Jev 拿下的 75 亿美元估值曾被质疑是一场泡沫。现在 Google 用一款多模态决策模型告诉市场：这不是泡沫，是赛道。

    作者丨郑佳美

    编辑丨岑  峰

谷歌正式入场了。

刚刚，谷歌发布 Gemini Decision 1，正式向 两个月前引爆决策模型品类的 TypeSafe Jev发起挑战。

和 Jev 一样，这款模型不生成任何文本，只计算供程序直接驱动 Agent 执行的候选项概率和置信度，不需要逐 Token 生成答案，连输出 Token 费用也省了。

更大的突破出现在并行计算上。Gemini Decision 1 可以在同一份上下文中处理至多 1000 项独立判断，而且支持文本、图像、音频、视频和 PDF 混合输入。对于需要反复检查文档、选择工具、评估任务状态的 Agent，大量原本分散在不同模型调用中的判断，现在可以集中在一轮请求中完成。

在数据上，7 项双方均有报告的共享基准中，Gemini Decision 1 赢下 5 项，Jev 在 When2Call 工具调用和 Mind2Web 多模态上仍保持优势（82.0% vs 79.9%，86.8% vs 86.2%）。

不过，Gemini 每 100 万输入 Token 收费 0.10 美元，是 Jev 的约 2.38 倍。性能上去了，价格也更贵了，谷歌显然想用更强的多模态能力和批量决策能力打开市场。

Jev 在 9 月发布后数周内拿下 75 亿美元估值，a16z 领投 8.7 亿美元，约三分之一财富 500 强被列为客户。但质疑从未消散：厂商自报的“快 193 倍、便宜 445 倍”缺乏第三方复现，原创性争议尚未定论，独立评测指向同一个结论：快和便宜是真的，质量是另一回事。雷峰网

Google 此时入场，至少证明了一件事：决策模型不是一场闹剧，而是一个值得巨头押注的品类。

**01**

**模型怎样跳过文本生成完成决策**

普通 LLM 处理“从四个工具里选一个”这类任务时，仍然走自回归解码：逐 Token 生成工具名或 JSON，程序再解析执行。模型承担的是开放式文本生成，业务需要的却是有限候选项中的概率判断。

Gemini Decision 1 把输出目标改成了候选项评分。开发者提前定义问题、候选集合和判断标准，模型读取输入后，直接返回各候选项的概率分布。整个过程通过单次前向计算完成，不需要逐 Token 生成答案，也没有输出 Token 费用。

这和普通的 Structured Output 有明显区别。Structured Output 仍然让模型生成文本，只是通过 Schema 限定 JSON 的字段和格式，Gemini Decision 1 则直接围绕有限候选空间完成评分，返回结果本身就是程序可以读取的数据。

这里有一个容易被忽略的细节：不同判断类型返回的概率含义并不相同。Noul 处理二元判断，返回某个条件成立的概率，范围为 0.01—0.99。如果问题本身存在歧义，开发者还可以分别定义什么情况算 Yes、什么情况算 No，减少判断标准不清晰带来的偏差。

Choice 处理多分类问题，支持 2—255 个候选项，返回胜出选项以及各候选项的归一化概率，所有候选项概率之和为 1。它适合工具路由、模型选择和任务分类。

不过，这种概率分配始终发生在给定的候选集合内，即使所有选项都不符合输入，模型仍会选出一个相对匹配的结果。因此，开发者需要提供 Other 选项，或者额外设置范围检查。

Score 的设计更有意思。它并不简单返回一个等级，而是先给有序评分标准中的每个等级分配概率，再计算加权评分。例如，将问题分为 0 级、1 级和 2 级，模型可能给出 0.1、0.7 和 0.2 的概率，最终评分可以落在 1 和 2 之间。

这实际上把离散分类扩展成了连续评分，方便程序进行排序和阈值筛选。不过，加权结果会压缩概率分布中的信息：两个输入即使得到相同分数，背后的等级概率也可能完全不同。因此，对于需要区分风险等级的任务，程序还应该读取各等级的概率，不能只使用最终评分。

这三种类型构成了 Gemini Decision 1 的输出体系。模型不再负责生成一段可以供人阅读的答案，开发者需要设计清晰的问题和候选标准，程序则负责把概率结果转化成具体执行条件。雷峰网

**02**

**1000 项问题如何完成独立计算**

Gemini Decision 1 的请求结构是一份 Shared Input 对应一组 Questions 。前者承载文本、图像、音频、视频和 PDF，后者定义需要完成的判断任务。每个问题可以使用不同的判断类型和评分标准，单次请求支持至多 1000 项问题。

以设备巡检为例，系统收到一段运行视频、一份维修记录和一段现场语音，需要判断设备是否异常、异常类别、严重程度以及是否需要人工检查。

开发者可以把三种材料放进同一份输入，再分别定义这些问题。异常检测使用 Noul，类别判断使用 Choice，严重程度使用 Score。模型读取相同材料，分别完成各项评分。

这套设计有两个技术细节。首先，每项问题具有独立的评估路径。Google 文档明确说明，各问题只能读取共享输入，不能读取其他问题的答案。

增加或删除某项问题，也不会改变其他问题的答案。这意味着并行评分没有依赖前序问题的推理链，模型可以在同一轮前向计算中完成多个独立判断。

其次，共享输入只计费一次。每项问题额外产生的费用来自自身的 instructions 和 criteria Token，而不需要重复计算整份材料。对于长文档批量审核、音视频检查和多维度内容评估，这种计费结构会影响整体调用成本。

但 1000 项问题并不意味着可以把任意复杂的工作流塞进一个请求。如果问题 B 必须根据问题 A 的具体结果生成新的候选项，两项任务就存在前后依赖。开发者需要先读取 A 的结果，再提交 B。

若 B 的候选项已经确定，只是需要在 A 不满足条件时忽略 B 的答案，则可以将两项判断同时提交，由程序决定是否采用结果。

输入长度同样需要考虑。Gemini Decision 1 的上下文上限为 256K Token，这个预算需要由共享材料和全部问题共同使用，并非每项问题各自拥有 256K。问题数量增加时，instructions 和 criteria 也会占用上下文空间。

谷歌公布的延迟数据中，在上下文不超过 16K Token 的测试条件下，从 1 项增加到 100 项问题，模型计算延迟基本保持平稳，中位计算延迟为 50—100 ms，端到端延迟为 150—250 ms。需要区分的是，API 支持 1000 项问题，公开的近乎平稳延迟测试范围则为 1—100 项。

多模态输入还涉及一项工程取舍。图像和视频可以设置 low、medium、high、ultra\_high 等分辨率等级，视觉细节越丰富，输入成本也会随之变化。

音频和 PDF 则直接进入相应的内容处理路径，无需开发者另外组织独立的识别服务。谷歌也明确将 OCR 和音频转写相关开销纳入模型输入计费体系，不另收输出 Token 费用。

这里并没有公开足够的信息来还原模型内部的并行计算图。能够确认的是，各问题共享同一份输入，在单次前向计算中独立评分。至于内部是否使用独立输出头、如何分配各问题的计算资源，谷歌目前没有给出完整技术说明。

**03**

**PK Jev：“五项领先”的背后**

Gemini Decision 1 为每项答案提供 confidence，取值为 0—1。它表示模型对当前结果正确性的估计。对于 Noul，confidence 取 Yes 和 No 两种结果中概率较高的一方，对于 Choice，它对应胜出选项的概率，对于 Score，则对应概率较高的等级。这项设计让程序能够根据判断可靠程度设置不同的执行门槛。

这里涉及概率校准。ECE（Expected Calibration Error，期望校准误差）衡量模型给出的概率与实际正确比例之间的偏差。谷歌公布的 Gemini Decision 1 ECE 为 0.0250，Jev 1.14 为 0.0494。

从产品落地来看，谷歌已经在 Gemini Notebook 中使用 Decisions API 进行模型路由，根据请求复杂程度选择模型档位和推理等级，日常请求延迟据称降低了 40%。

Google Search 将其用于 MCP 工具的安全检查，Stitch 则使用它加快交互设计过程中的操作选择。与 TypeSafe Jev 相比，两款模型的技术方向相近，但公开信息呈现出不同侧重。

TypeSafe 已经披露 Jev 使用专门的模型架构、Parallel Sampler，以及 RLCD（Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions）训练方法。Jev 1.14 增加了图像输入、Box 判断类型和长上下文能力，不过相关功能在发布时仍被放在实验性配置中。

Gemini Decision 1 则依托 Gemini 原生多模态架构，将音频、视频、PDF 纳入输入范围，并提供 256K 上下文和 1000 项问题请求能力。谷歌尚未披露与 TypeSafe 类似的训练方案，因此两者的内部训练路线暂时无法进行直接比较。

性能上，谷歌公布的 7 项共享基准中，Gemini Decision 1 有 5 项超过 Jev 1.14，Jev 在 When2Call 工具调用和 Mind2Web 多模态上保持领先。When2Call 是 Agent 工具选择的核心场景，Jev 在这个指标上的反超说明 Google 的优势并非无差别覆盖。

另外，第三方独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的 Decision Index v2.1 榜单中， Gemini Decision 1 的综合分 65.98，略低于 Jev 的 66.23，远低于榜首 Drex Max v1.1 的 72.62。单任务延迟 211 ms，高于 Jev 的 92 ms；价格方面，Gemini 每 100 万输入 Token 收费 0.10 美元，Jev 为 0.042 美元。

换句话说，Google 用多模态能力和批量处理换溢价，但“更强”在第三方统一任务套件上尚未兑现为“更优”。校准误差的领先是真实的，但校准领先不等于综合决策质量领先。

**04**

**Agent 的决策层，正在变成独立战场**

Gemini Decision 1 把原本散落在 Agent 工作流中的一类任务，正式变成了独立的模型调用能力。它涉及的不只是评分速度，还包括候选空间定义、共享输入复用、问题隔离、概率校准和程序控制之间的配合。

通用 LLM 仍然负责复杂推理、规划和内容生成，Decision Model 则承担能够提前定义标准的判断任务。开发者需要根据任务依赖关系安排调用顺序，再根据概率表现决定自动执行范围。

Jev 在 9 月点燃了这个品类，Google 在 11 月用多模态和批量能力加注。这条路线能否形成长期优势，还要看模型在复杂输入、任务分布变化和真实业务环境中的稳定表现。谷歌入场后，专用决策模型开始进入更大规模的产品竞争，Agent 的工程设计也将从单纯依赖生成模型，转向更加细致的模型分工。

*参考链接：**https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-decisions-api/*

items.title: 诺亦腾机器人入选 The Information 2026 全球最具潜力50家初创企业榜单
items.content:
核心要点（Key Facts）

· 在 The Information 于 11 月 11 日发布的“2026 全球最具潜力 50 家初创企业”榜单中，诺亦腾机器人（Noitom Robotics）位列亚洲分区第一。

· 根据榜单披露，诺亦腾机器人目前估值已超 5 亿美元，累计股权融资逾 5000 万美元，年营收突破 1000 万美元。

· 诺亦腾机器人致力于生产供机器人学习的人类数据。公司在中国深圳和美国加州山景城设有数据工厂，并已与物理 AI（Physical AI）领域的近百家企业展开合作。

新加坡，2026年11月18日 —— 全球知名科技商业媒体 The Information 近日正式发布"The 50 Most Promising Startups 2026"榜单（全球最具潜力50家初创企业）。物理 AI 数据公司诺亦腾机器人（Noitom Robotics）在亚洲顶尖初创企业榜单（Top Asia Startups）中名列第一。

Fig 1. The Information 2026 全球最具潜力50家初创企业榜单

榜单数据显示，诺亦腾机器人当前估值已超5亿美元，股权融资总额超5000万美元，营收超1000万美元。

The Information 创办于2013年，重点覆盖科技、人工智能与金融，面向全球60多个国家的商业领袖与专业读者提供原创独家报道和深度分析。The Information 50 榜单旨在发掘各细分赛道中最具龙头潜力的早期初创企业，围绕营收规模、商业模式及增长前景进行严格评估，相关财务数据由记者直接向创始人和投资人采集。

诺亦腾机器人创始人兼CEO戴若犁博士表示：

"The Information 依据营收和增长表现对初创企业进行排名。去年，机器人研发团队对人类动作数据的需求还在千小时量级；今年，这一需求已跃升至数十万小时。同时对这些团队而言，另一个至关重要的问题是：具身模型能否真正从这些数据中学到东西。我们很高兴诺亦腾机器人能够获得 The Information 的认可。此次入选，也印证了解决'数据规模'与'数据可学习性'这两大痛点的巨大商业价值。"

不造机器人，专注生产机器人学习的"数据"

诺亦腾机器人并不制造机器人。公司专注于生产驱动机器人进化的高质量训练数据——通过自建数据工厂与广泛的线下合作场景，系统化采集人类动作、物体交互及日常行为数据，并通过旗下数据平台 ModalityNet（modalitynet.com），向全球机器人本体厂商与 AI 开发者提供标准化的多模态数据集。

2025年正式分拆成立后，诺亦腾机器人凭借团队长达13年的动作捕捉技术积淀，快速构建起全球化的数据产能与服务网络。目前公司规模已超百人，在深圳和美国加州山景城（Mountain View）设有数据工厂，在台北和吉隆坡设有数据采集中心，正积极向全球其他地区拓展。截至目前，公司已与物理 AI 领域近百家企业及研发机构达成深度合作。

过去一年融资、产品及研发里程碑不断

此次入围 The Information 50，源于过去一年间公司在融资、产品及研发领域接连达成的一系列里程碑成果：

2025年11月 — 公司完成由阿尔法公社领投，经纬创投（MPCi）、英诺天使基金等机构跟投的 Pre-A 轮融资。

2025年12月 — 公司完成由启明创投领投，阿尔法公社、经纬创投、五源资本等跟投的 Pre-A+ 轮融资。

2026年6月 — 诺亦腾机器人正式发布数据平台 ModalityNet，三大旗舰数据集产品同步上线。同期宣布完成数亿元人民币 Pre-A++ 轮融资，获北京市人工智能产业投资基金（顺禧管理）、上海人工智能产业系列基金、深创投等多家头部产业资本，以及阿尔法公社、君联资本、五源资本、经纬创投等老股东超额认购。

2026年8月 — 高精度人机交互数据集 HiPHI（High Precision Human Interaction）上线，面向学术科研社区开放。HiPHI 是 HiPHI-MOV（Motion with Object and Vision，含物体与视觉的运动数据）语料库的开放研究子集，依据 ModalityNet 开放研究许可证（MORL v1.0）免费供研究使用，完整 HiPHI-MOV 语料库通过 ModalityNet 进行商业授权。目前在 Hugging Face 及公司分发渠道下载量已突破15,000次。

2026年11月 — 在奥斯汀举办的机器人学习大会（CoRL 2026）上，诺亦腾机器人团队三篇论文获主会收录，同期重磅推出全新类别的真实场景人类数据集 ITW-Ego Plus，并公开了 HiPHI 系列的第二个开放研究数据集 HiPHI-Hand，该数据集已被用于 NVIDIA EgoHand 模型的训练。

Fig 2. 诺亦腾机器人真实场景数据集 ITW-EGO Plus 数据可视化效果

关于此次 The Information 50 的完整榜单已面向 The Information 订阅用户发布。 <https://www.theinformation.com/projects/the-information-50-2026>.

关于诺亦腾机器人

诺亦腾机器人是一家专注于 Physical AI 的数据公司。公司致力于打造"世界编译器"（World Compiler）——将真实世界的人类交互转化为可供机器学习的基础设施层，为具身智能提供可被机器学习的表征。其核心实现为 ModalityNet（modalitynet.com），一个大规模、以人为中心的全模态数据底座，建立在三大互补数据体系之上：

· HiPHI-MOV（High Precision Human Interaction — Motion with Object and Vision，高精度人机交互-含物体与视觉的运动数据）：采集高保真全身运动与移动操作数据；

· HiPHI-OM（High Precision Human Interaction — Omni-Manipulation，高精度人机交互-全模态灵巧操作）：采集包含接触、力、触觉及物体状态信号在内的全模态交互数据；

· ITW-EgoVision & Ego Plus（In-The-Wild，真实场景数据）：在非受控真实环境中大规模采集自然人类行为数据。

三大数据体系共同应对物理 AI 的核心瓶颈。诺亦腾机器人始终不变的使命：让物理世界可被学习。

items.title: 黄仁勋「每天都在用」的 Perplexity 开始重构 Attention，把「判断」做成了一个独立模型
items.content:
Decider v1.3：63 项分类任务准确率达 91.6%，对标 Jev 成本直降 61%。

    作者丨郑佳美

    编辑丨岑   峰

刚刚，黄仁勋每天都在用的「AI 导师」 Perplexity 有了新动作：正式推出 Decider v1.3，直接把 AI 系统里的判断能力单独做成了一套模型。

Perplexity 这次直接改了模型处理判断任务的方式：**同一份上下文可以同时交给多个问题使用，模型只需进行一次前向传播，就能输出各个问题的答案概率。** 过去需要反复调用 LLM、生成文本、解析结果的流程，现在可以收敛到一次模型计算中。

为了让多个问题共享计算时不互相干扰，Perplexity 还重新设计了 Attention 机制，让共享状态读取全部问题，同时限制问题之间直接交换信息。v1.3 进一步加入 Locate 能力，可以根据字段描述直接定位原文跨度，将判断与文本抽取整合进同一套架构。

这套模型已经进入 Perplexity 的生产系统。在一次内部安全审查中，它单日处理了 7000 个 Agent 会话，累计读取 10 亿 token，并推动 14 项规则修复。

从技术架构来看，Decider 有三个紧密关联的设计层次：输入端如何把共享上下文与独立问题组织在一起，注意力层如何控制不同问题的信息交互，训练与输出层又如何让同一套模型兼顾分类判断和文本定位。

**其中，隔离式问题注意力改变了多任务共享计算的底层方式，也是理解整个 Decider 架构的关键切口。**

**01**

**一份上下文，承载多个判断任务**

Decider 的输入其实是由共享状态（State）和若干问题块（Question）组成。State 保存网页、文档或 Agent 执行记录，Question 描述具体判断目标，并列出候选答案。每个候选项映射到预定义标签 Token，例如 A、B、C，特殊的 <|marker|> Token 则标记答案读取位置。

模型处理时，会提取 Marker 对应位置的隐藏状态，交给决策头计算各候选项的分数，再转换为概率分布。

这里的决策头由基础模型原有的语言模型输出层改造而来：Perplexity 保留 A、B、C 等候选标签对应的权重行，移除其余词表输出权重，再针对决策任务进行训练。原本用于计算下一个 Token 概率的输出层，由此转为专门处理选项判断。

这个设计让任务定义与输出计算分离。调用方可以通过自然语言描述问题，通过选项限定答案空间，模型则负责根据上下文计算各选项的概率。

情感分析、自然语言推理、意图检测、实体匹配、内容审核、事实核查和评分，可以采用同一套输入协议，不需要为每种任务单独建立一套模型结构。

Perplexity 将数百个公开数据集转换为 State、Question、选项和目标组成的统一训练格式。训练目标既可以是正确标签，也可以是完整的答案概率分布。对于同一段长文本需要执行多项判断的情况，多个 Question 可以放进同一次前向传播，模型只需处理一份共享上下文。

不过计算收益需要准确理解：增加问题仍然会增加 Question Token 和注意力计算，Decider 节省的主要是长文本被重复编码的开销，以及生成式模型逐 Token 解码和外部解析的成本。问题数量越多、共享文本越长，复用价值越明显。

输出概率还保留了业务策略的调整空间。模型负责给出候选项的概率分布，应用根据误报、漏报的业务代价设置阈值。网页过滤和 Agent 执行审查可以使用不同门槛，无需为每种业务重新训练决策模型。

**02**

**多任务如何共享信息，互不干扰**

输入协议确定后，新的问题落在模型内部：多个 Question 同时进入 Transformer，它们之间应该建立怎样的信息连接？

Decider 以生成式 LLM 为骨干，原有因果注意力按照文本顺序组织信息，当前位置只能读取自身及前面的 Token。这种结构适合逐步生成文本，却不利于需要理解完整上下文的判断任务。

Perplexity 因此改用双向注意力，让 Token 可以读取完整输入。消融实验显示，这项调整改善了模型的决策表现。

双向注意力开放了完整上下文，但也让多个问题之间出现信息交互。v1.2 使用完全互见模式，State 和全部 Question 可以相互读取。这样一来，某个问题的表示可能受到其他问题的影响，调用方调整问题组合时，原有判断也可能随之变化。

v1.3 引入的 Isolated Question Attention 改变了这套连接关系：State 可以读取全部 Question，而每个 Question 只能读取 State 和自身 Token，不能直接读取其他问题。

这里有一个关键细节：State 不再只是保存原始文本的容器，它还承担了跨任务的信息汇聚作用。它可以读取整组问题，在多层注意力计算中形成包含任务条件的上下文表示，每个 Question 则通过 State 获取相关信息，并保留自身的任务描述。

这种结构切断了 Question 之间直接传递局部表示的路径，但没有消除全部间接影响。由于 State 已经读取其他问题的信息，经过多层 Transformer 的传播，问题 A 的信息仍可能先进入 State 的后续表示，再被问题 B 读取。

Perplexity 控制的是直接注意力连接，而非让各项任务在数学意义上完全独立。这个区别也解释了为什么 v1.3 没有选择完全可缓存模式。团队测试过另一种结构：State 只读取自身内容，Question 再读取 State 和自身 Token。雷峰网

这样同一段文本可以在不同请求之间复用缓存，因为 State 表示不依赖具体问题集合。但代价是 State 编码时看不到任务要求，无法根据当前问题调整上下文表示。Perplexity 最终选择隔离式问题注意力，保留问题对上下文的条件作用。

团队还通过标签扰动测试检验输出稳定性。在 372 道多项选择题上，改变选项顺序、标签映射和标签名称后，Decider v1.3 只有 0.27% 的问题发生语义答案变化，Jev 1.14 的变化比例为 2.69% 至 4.84%。相同输入重复执行时，Decider v1.3 的输出保持一致。

隔离式注意力由此成为 Decider 的核心架构设计：它决定了共享上下文怎样参与多项判断，也决定了不同问题之间可以通过哪些路径交换信息。

**03**

**从选项判断，到文本跨度抽取**

普通决策头的输出范围由预设选项限定。当任务要求模型从原文中找出一段未知长度的文本时，仅靠 A、B、C 这样的标签已经无法满足需求。Decider v1.3 因此增加 Locate，将输出扩展到文本跨度定位。

Locate 新增了 <|locate|> Token、跨度头（Span Head）和 LoRA 适配器。每个待抽取字段拥有独立的 Locate Token，其嵌入由此前训练得到的 Marker 表示初始化。跨度头结合 Locate Token 与 State 中各 Token 的隐藏表示，对候选文本片段的起点、终点及两端配对关系进行评分，同时为字段生成专属阈值。

起点与终点评分负责寻找文本边界，配对评分则判断两个位置能否组成有效片段。单独找到两个高分位置，并不意味着它们一定属于同一段合理文本，因此配对关系也需要独立学习。模型返回原文字符区间，下游程序可以直接读取对应内容。leifengwan

训练采用改进版 InfoNCE 目标，让正确跨度的分数高于阈值，同时让阈值高于其他候选跨度。当原文没有对应字段时，模型需要将阈值抬高，使候选片段无法通过筛选，进而返回空列表。

Perplexity 使用命名实体识别、PII 检测和抽取式问答数据训练 Locate，字段描述既有简短标签，也有自然语言指令。这样的数据组织让模型需要理解字段含义与文本内容之间的关系，而非只记忆固定字段名称。

Locate 也带来了参数干扰问题。原有决策头学习候选选项之间的概率分布，跨度头学习文本边界和片段配对，两种任务对模型内部表示的要求存在差异。

Perplexity 发现，将 Locate 适配器合并进主干后，普通决策请求会出现退化，因此保留独立 LoRA 适配器，只在文本定位任务中启用。

主模型采用分阶段训练。较大版本以 Qwen3.8-27B 为基础，先进行大规模通用全量微调，并排除公开评测基准的训练划分，随后通过 LoRA 加入领域任务，再进行视觉适配。团队对三个不同随机种子的文本训练权重取平均，以改善模型整体表现。

Flash 版本以 Qwen3.5-4B 为基础，通过较大 Decider 蒸馏获得能力。学生模型拟合教师给出的完整概率分布，通过 KL 散度学习教师对不同候选项的相对判断。雷峰网

相比只学习正确标签，分布蒸馏还保留了其他候选项的相对置信程度。Perplexity 表示，在相同训练数据下，KL 蒸馏在留出任务上的泛化表现优于标准交叉熵目标。

评测中，Decider v1.3 在 63 项分类任务上的平均准确率为 91.6%，比 Perplexity 原有生产分类器高 6.54 个百分点，在 72 项检索任务中，逐点重排的平均 nDCG@10 达到 83.99，比 Qwen3-Reranker-8B 高 1.81 分。

八种语言任务的平均准确率为 88.16%，Jev 1.14 为 85.41%。Locate 在 17 项域外任务上的平均得分为 69.0，Flash 为 63.6。生产评估覆盖 API 上线后前 18 天的一百万条请求，去重后包含 2,318,887 个问题。由于生产请求缺少人工标注，团队使用前沿 LLM 评判模型生成参考答案。

Decider v1.3 与参考答案的一致性为 93.98%，略高于 v1.2 的 93.68% 和 Jev 1.14 的 93.35%。这项数据反映模型与评判模型的吻合程度，但不能直接等同于人工标注下的真实准确率。

**04**

**判断，开始拥有独立计算架构**

Decider 的技术路线围绕一个明确问题展开：如何让模型在保留上下文理解能力的同时，高效处理大量结构化判断。它通过输入协议、隔离式注意力和 Locate 扩展，建立了从选项判断到文本定位的完整能力体系。

但这套架构仍有边界。目前公开的评测结果展示了它在分类、检索重排和文本抽取上的表现，生产案例也说明 Perplexity 已经将其用于内部工作流程。

不过，模型的实际收益仍然取决于任务类型、上下文长度、并行问题数量和部署成本。现有数据还不足以说明这种架构适合所有 AI 应用，尤其是开放式推理和复杂规划，通用 LLM 仍然有自己的优势。

对于 Agent 系统，Decider 确实是提供了一种值得继续验证的分工思路：让通用 LLM 处理复杂理解与生成，将边界清楚的分类、筛选和评估交给专门模型。但两者能否形成更合适的协作方式，还需要结合真实工作负载中的延迟、资源消耗和任务表现进一步检验。

*参考链接：**https://www.perplexity.ai/en-GB/hub/blog/perplexity-decider*

items.title: Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin With PVTW
items.content:
Production test is necessarily built around decisions. PASS. FAIL. Bin 1. Bin 2. Ship. Do not ship. Characterization has a different objective. It asks not only whether the device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary.

That distinction becomes increasingly important as processors integrate compute, memory, high speed interfaces, multiple power domains and advanced packaging into increasingly complex systems.

Suppose five devices all pass the product specification, but under the same controlled workload their minimum stable operating voltages are:

0.70 V | 0.71 V | 0.73 V | 0.76 V | 0.79 V

Production test sees five passing devices. Characterization sees five different levels of margin. That changes the engineering question from “Why did this device fail?” to something potentially much more useful:

**What is consuming product margin?**

PVTW (process, voltage, temperature, workload) gives us a framework for exploring that question.

Take the same device and establish its voltage and frequency boundary using conventional ATE content. Then establish another boundary while running a deterministic compute workload. Repeat with SRAM, memory, PCIe and combined workloads. We may discover that the boundaries are different.

That difference can tell us which workload is exposing the limiting condition and where deeper characterization should begin.

## Characterize the boundary

Rather than testing at one nominal operating point, deliberately approach the boundary. Sweep voltage at fixed frequency, temperature and workload. Sweep frequency while the other conditions remain fixed. Repeat across temperature. Then manipulate individual power domains.

A compute workload may be characterized while the core rail is swept and memory and I/O rails remain fixed. A memory-intensive workload can be characterized while a memory-related rail is swept. PCIe traffic can be maintained while relevant electrical and thermal conditions are changed.

Now we are not simply determining whether a subsystem functions. We are measuring how much margin it has under a defined workload.

## Known good versus marginal populations

Population analysis makes this more powerful. Take known good devices and devices showing reduced SLT margin. Characterize both populations under identical PVTW conditions. Instead of asking only which devices fail, compare the shapes of their operating envelopes.

Does the marginal population show a consistent voltage shift? Does the difference emerge only at high temperature? Does it appear only under simultaneous compute and memory activity? Is there a particular rail or frequency transition where the two populations separate?

The shape of the margin distribution can provide clues to the physical mechanism.

## A long SLT failure can become a short test

Suppose a particular system workload requires 45 minutes before marginal devices begin generating errors. That is useful for learning, but expensive as a production screen.

PVTW characterization can help determine why that workload exposes the problem. Once the mechanism is better understood, the ATE capability can search for a shorter electrical, structural or functional signature correlated with the same marginality.

Perhaps a voltage and frequency corner exposes it in seconds. Perhaps a targeted functional pattern reproduces the condition. Perhaps a particular power rail response or interface measurement predicts it.

If the correlation is strong enough, the shorter test can potentially move into Final Test or even Wafer Sort. The learning flow becomes:

SLT discovers → PVTW characterizes → ATE correlates → Production test screens

The goal of deeper SLT characterization is therefore not necessarily more SLT. In some cases, its greatest value may be teaching us how to screen the risk earlier and faster.

## Margin is a continuous engineering variable

This is why I believe we should preserve margin data rather than reducing everything immediately to PASS and FAIL. Minimum operating voltage, maximum stable frequency, thermal margin, interface margin, power margin and workload margin can all become continuous characterization parameters. Those measurements can be compared across device populations, process corners, assembly conditions and eventually manufacturing history.

A device with 100 mV of margin and a device with 10 mV of margin may both satisfy the production specification today. But they may tell us very different things about process variation, product robustness and future design decisions. Characterizing those differences can help answer a more fundamental question:

**Where is the product operating boundary, and what moves it?**

That question does not end at the silicon. The package surrounding the silicon has its own manufacturing history, materials and process variation.

In Part 3, I will explore how 2D ID and unit level traceability could connect PVTW margin all the way back to wafer X,Y and substrate panel X,Y.

- [Part 1: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload](https://semiengineering.com/pvtw-extending-silicon-characterization-from-pvt-to-real-world-workload/)

The post [Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin With PVTW](https://semiengineering.com/beyond-pass-fail-characterizing-silicon-margin-with-pvtw/) appeared first on [Semiconductor Engineering](https://semiengineering.com).

items.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
items.content:
**Key Takeaways:**

- AI accelerators and GPUs consume thousands of amperes at increasingly low voltages, causing a shift to vertical power delivery that brings regulation closer to loads.
- Advances in integrated voltage regulators and passive components are enabling new power architectures.
- Power delivery is becoming a system-level co-design challenge, expanding simulation needs and the role of OSATs.

---

Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.

To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.

The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while slashing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. That approach is being extended with increasingly sophisticated on-die decoupling capacitors (DCaps) formed in deep trenches as part of the BPDN. While this addresses high-frequency decoupling at the chip level, recent changes inside packages, interposers, substrates, and across data center racks are becoming just as important.

Add to that recent developments in the design of compact passive devices, like high-performance inductors, and new architectural solutions become possible, moving the VRMs and DC-DC converters into the interposer or package.

But these architectural changes are neither straightforward nor simple because they involve system co-design of the PDN, interposer, power management ICs (PMICs), integrated voltage regulators (IVRs), DC-DC converters, capacitors, and other passive devices, alongside custom HPC, memory devices, and interconnects that perform today’s elaborate AI tasks.

“In the most advanced semiconductors, people are moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs. Those IVRs are great because they are placed much closer to the chip, which reduces the IR drop to the chip’s own power delivery network, so it is way more efficient. In addition, closed and fast control loops between the chip power management unit to the IVR reduce the reaction time to voltage droop events from milliseconds to microseconds. Because this reaction is so fast you can tune voltage very accurately, with a high degree of granularity even on different areas of a chip,” said Nir Sever, senior director of business development at [proteanTecs](https://semiengineering.com/entities/proteantecs/).

Reconfiguring the PDN is part of a much larger drive to improve energy use. “Energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward,” said Lipen Yuan, senior director of TSMC’s Advanced Technology Business Development, during a 2024 IEDM short course.

Power delivery challenges are most important at points of load. “AI systems are placing unprecedented demands on board-to-chip power delivery, making the final stage of voltage regulation increasingly important,” said CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at [ASE](https://semiengineering.com/entities/ase/).

**Fig. 1: By regulating voltage at the point of load, OSATs enable fine-tuned voltage control. Source: ASE**

“The move to multi-die architectures is bringing power integrity to the forefront, alongside thermal, stress, and warpage challenges. But the underlying power-delivery problem already existed in advanced single-die designs,” said Sojan Philips, principal product manager of Redhawk-SC at [Synopsys](https://semiengineering.com/entities/synopsys-inc/). “AI accelerators are now operating at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the power-delivery network can result in significant IR drop. That loss of voltage margin can directly affect performance and power targets, particularly maximum operating frequency and Vmin.”

Several developments illustrate these trends:

- **Backside PDN**: Intel Foundry’s 18A was the first to move backside wafer processing into leading-edge high-volume manufacturing. Samsung and TSMC plan to implement backside PDNs at future advanced nodes, starting next year.
- **Integrated voltage regulators**: ASE, Marvell, Empower, and others are moving voltage regulation closer to the processor.
- **Embedded capacitors and inductors**: Integration of compact passive components is becoming a key differentiator in high-density power delivery.
- **Co-optimization of package and on-chip power**: Power integrity can no longer be optimized independently at the PCB, substrate, interposer, and transistor levels.

As a result, OSATs are playing an increasing role in system co-design, electrical validation, and power integrity (PI) simulation. “The OSAT sits where die, substrate or interposer, passives, and board meet, so we are brought in earlier to model the package-level PDN and co-simulate it with the customer’s die power data,” said Alex Kizeev, technical director of signal and power integrity at [Amkor’s](https://semiengineering.com/entities/amkor-technology/) design optimization team.

Kizeev breaks down the supply chain and responsibilities among different companies. “The best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board. The foundry and fabless teams own the on-die PDN, including the die power map and the bump-map allocation. The substrate supplier defines what stackup and via/plane technology is possible. The OSAT optimizes the package-level pieces, including stackup choice, via and ball assignment, DCap selection and placement, warpage and reliability, and validation.”

“Backside power delivery can significantly improve power delivery by reducing IR drop and freeing up frontside routing resources for signals, but it doesn’t eliminate power-integrity challenges,” said Philips. “It also changes the thermal landscape. As power delivery and other structures move to the backside, the paths available for heat removal become more complex. This makes co-optimization of power integrity and thermal management increasingly important.

The overall trend is moving toward closer integration in advanced packages and dies, including the integration of inductors, capacitors, and power-conversion components into substrates and interposers.

**Why power losses scale with increasing power**
A simple illustration shows how the power efficiency drops as the industry scales from a 1kW GPU to a 5kW GPU (see figure 2). While losses from the voltage regulator itself stay constant at around 13%, resistive losses jump from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rises from 17% to 31%. As a result, increasing power levels must be supplied to meet all the chip-level needs.

**Fig. 2: At higher power levels, the PDN efficiency using motherboard voltage regulators degrades significantly due to VR losses, resistive losses, and droop. Source: Intel Foundry**

With this lateral power delivery approach, power integrity (PI) becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as compute loads rise. As AI accelerators integrate increasing levels of compute, HBM, and interconnects between devices, the low supply voltage (0.7-0.9V) of devices means multiple kiloamp levels of current are needed to meet the high-power needs of modern GPUs. As if managing kiloamp currents is not enough, fast workload transients tend to magnify voltage droop, so designers apply voltage guardbands that further increase power consumption and reduce system efficiency. [1]

**Next-gen data centers pull in 800V**
For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands, 800V DC power delivery is starting to replace traditional AC power distribution. The 800V DC power distribution coexists with multiple distributed regulators located much closer to individual loads.

To lower transmission losses from the grid to the microprocessor, next-generation PDNs begin at 800V DC and are stepped down in stages using DC-to-DC converters to 48V, 12V, and then 0.7V, for instance. One of the most critical junctures occurs at the point of load, where integrated voltage regulators supply the AI multi-chiplet package. By limiting the number of power conversions, system-level efficiency can improve while reducing thermal cooling requirements.

The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB, a logical first step that is commonly referred to as vertical power delivery. However, chipmakers are embracing recent developments that shrink the size of various voltage regulator components, especially capacitors and inductors, to move voltage regulation inside the main processor package and below the SoC, called integrated power delivery. Finally, integrating voltage regulator components into the interposer itself is called fully integrated power delivery.

**One step at a time**
The approach companies take to voltage regulation integration depends on the company’s expertise, its partners, and the complexity of the system involved.

For this reason, companies are introducing suites of solutions. For example, ASE is offering a range of power delivery capabilities to enable PCB backside integration, which considers the limited space inside computer trays. [2] The company’s PowerSiP options can include double-sided connected capacitors sandwiched between coreless substrates; substrateless designs, solder-free cap array modules with exposed terminals for embedded substrate or PCB solutions; high-aspect-ratio 4:1 copper pin integration for lower packaging impedance; and high-density active and passive component integration using single- or double-sided molding.

“Power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge for next-generation AI systems,” said Harrison Chang, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE. “By shortening the high-current transmission path, our solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more, translating directly into meaningful power savings at the system level,” he said in the release.

In June 2025, Marvell introduced its Package Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR) technology for AI and HPC. The PIVR replaces the conventional arrangement of discrete voltage-regulator components, often several inches away on the PCB, with compact silicon power converters and passive components tightly coupled to the processor. It’s designed to reduce the amount of low-voltage, high-current routing between the regulator and the processor. The PIVR can sit on the underside of the processor package, shortening the path from voltage conversion to the processor’s power connections. It also can sit next to the processor’s package or inside the advanced package.

Marvell is partnering with multiple companies on integration, including Infineon, which makes power semiconductors and packaged devices; Ferric, which specializes in designing integrated voltage regulators using thin-film magnetic inductors; Monolithic Power Systems, a developer of high-current-density power modules; and Empower Semiconductor, a developer of compact integrated power converters.

In July of this year, Analog Devices completed the acquisition of Empower Semiconductor, expanding ADI’s AI compute power delivery capabilities with integrated voltage regulators and silicon capacitors. “By enabling power conversion closer to the processor, the combined solution shortens the power delivery path and improves efficiency to support higher-performance, higher-density systems. Building on its leadership in high-performance power management, ADI is investing in its system-level platform to deliver a step-change in performance, density, and efficiency from grid to core.” [3]

In addition, on Nov. 2, onsemi announced it will acquire the assets of Ferric, which develops integrated voltage regulators, for up to $775 million. [4]

To understand these important acquisitions, it helps to take a closer look at IVRs.

**What is an IVR?**
An integrated voltage regulator is typically a 3D stack arrangement that replaces off-chip voltage regulator modules and bulky capacitors and inductors on the PCB with integrated magnetics and passives mounted onto the silicon or package using thin-film technology.

“The IVR is implemented as a 3D stack, bringing together the deep-trench capacitor, PMIC, and inductor, and embedding them directly into the substrate or interposer,” said Veshal Sridhar, product engineering architect, 3D IC at Synopsys. “Companies are moving it closer to the SOC for obvious reasons such as reduced signal parasitics between IVR and SOC die, but that introduces new thermal effects and stress effects because you’re bringing another 3D stack in and embedding it inside an interposer. There’s also potential noise coupling into the other dies from the IVR, because even for a simple 3D stack you are going to have noise coupling.”

In what Intel Foundry refers to as a Super High Density MIM (metal-insulator-metal), capacitance density can be improved by 10× compared to conventional MIM capacitors. [5] This may offer response times on the order of nanoseconds. As part of Intel’s collaboration with UMC for 12nm finFETs, the capacitors feature three metal layers for routing in a scalable design. “This broad adaptability highlights the HDMIM as a universal, highly scalable passive component, capable of heterogeneous integration with logic and power chips manufactured across diverse process nodes from various foundries.” [5]

Inductors have traditionally been one of the greatest passive bottlenecks due to their large footprint, but by integrating them into the package using copper-plated through-hole technology and advanced magnetic materials (see Figure 3), Intel is touting a high resistance-to-capacitance ratio while minimizing stray magnetic fields that could adversely affect surrounding circuits. [5]

**Fig. 3: This in-package inductor uses copper-plated through holes embedded with high-permeability magnetics to improve the resistance-to-capacitance ratio and limit magnetic parasitic effects. Source: Intel Foundry**

Intel’s FIVR platform uses switched-capacitor voltage regulators and hybrid buck converters to accommodate nanosecond transient spikes by computing cores without exacerbating voltage droop. FIVRs that allow a continuous switching range are superior to fixed SCVRs when it comes to delivering low-voltage inputs (e.g., 1.8 to 3V).

Finally, Intel’s low-voltage GaN MOSHEMT-on-CMOS devices are designed for >12V applications, where high density and high efficiency are essential, while minimizing the overall number of power conversions. By integrating both low voltage and high voltage MIM capacitors with active devices, it minimizes PDN impedance from VR to load. By monolithically integrating the GaN power switches with GaN nMOS drivers, the company can achieve even faster response to transients along with aggressive power density.

“Integrated voltage regulators provide unprecedented speed and granularity in voltage control, but realizing their full power-saving potential requires equally precise visibility into the silicon itself,” said proteanTecs’ Sever. “Traditional power management methods leave significant timing margin untapped. By continuously measuring timing margins across the full chip, cycle by cycle, under actual operating conditions, our embedded monitoring technology identifies where performance is truly limited and where voltage can be safely reduced. Combined with the fine-grained control of IVRs, this enables more aggressive power optimization without compromising performance or reliability.”

**Can the system handle the power?**
Multiphysics simulation plays an important role in power delivery planning. “A designer may have a simple stack in mind, interposer, base die, top die, and substrate. And it starts with a prototype grid and listing the power required for each die,” explained Synopsys’ Sridhar. “So there is a power budget that comes from the devices, and number of C4 bumps, number of microbumps, TSVs, etc. You want to determine whether your power delivery system can deliver the power needed from the C4 bumps through the top of the stack. Starting with a simple static IR-drop analysis, we can then leverage 3DIC Compiler together with signoff solutions like RedHawk-SC to help bridge the gap between early bump planning and PSE (power sourcing equipment) planning.”

In cases where the PDN cannot handle the power required of the system, design changes such as increasing the interposer size may come into play.

Sridhar noted how one customer brought system-level PI (power integrity) analysis into the early architecture stage, closing the loop between implementation and system analysis using 3DICC plus RHSC, turning iterations that once took days into hours and giving designers more freedom to explore before the architecture is frozen.

At the same time, the package assembly design kits that OSATs compile are becoming more detailed. “Kits are moving beyond geometric design rules to include electrical models, material properties, and validated reference designs. Teams now must consider bump pitch against current density, metal layers against cost, and DCap placement against thermal path early in the design,” said Amkor’s Kizeev.

**Conclusion**
Power integrity and power efficiency have already become key differentiators in advanced AI accelerator-based data center designs. Companies are racing to incorporate leading power delivery solutions, including integrated voltage regulators, in positions closer to the GPU or AI accelerator modules where they can be most effective. Advanced power delivery began with the integration of wafer backside PDNs, but package-level and interposer-level solutions are coming fast.

Coordination among major companies in the supply chain is critical during early-stage PDN design. “Some of these design houses are not building the entire system, for instance, like HBM, where even the base die and the stack may be coming in from other design houses,” noted Synopsys’ Phillips. They want to make sure that the grid they’re designing in-house works with the other models. So they want a model exchange between these two, which is performed as part of a feasibility analysis.”

**References**

1. Radhakrishnan, V. Javvaji and N. Butzen, “Driving Power Delivery Innovations for the AI Data Center Era,” Intel Foundry, https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/central-libraries/us/en/documents/2026-08/foundry-power-delivery-white-paper.pdf
2. “ASE Expands PowerSiP Platform for Next-Generation AI Power Delivery,” press release, October 13, 2026, https://ase.aseglobal.com/press-room/ase-expands-powersip-platform-for-next-generation-ai-power-delivery/
3. <https://www.analog.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026/5-19-2026>
4. “onsemi to Acquire Ferric, Establishing Leadership in Power Delivery for Next-Generation AI Processors,” November 2, 2026. https://www.onsemi.com/company/newsroom/news-and-insights/onsemi-to-acquire-ferric-establishing-leadership-in-power-delivery-for-next-generation-ai-processors/
5. Yu et al., “Vertical Power Delivery for 5 kW AI Systems: From Advanced Passives to GaN IC Integration,” 2026 IEEE 38th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD), Las Vegas, NV, USA, 2026, pp. 337-340, doi: 10.1109/ISPSD64561.2026.11553768.

items.title: How Virtual Twins And Machine Learning Optimize DRAM Yield
items.content:
As memory technologies continue to scale, manufacturing processes are becoming increasingly complex.

Additional process steps, tighter process windows, and new sources of variation are making it progressively more challenging to reach acceptable yield.

Systemic failures are emerging as a source of yield loss during yield ramp. Unlike random defects, these failures are often driven by complex interactions between multiple process modules.

Rapid root-cause identification of these systemic defects is critical to quickly improving yield and accelerating time-to-market.1 But conventional failure analysis relies heavily on wafer experimentation and statistical analysis, which can be slow and costly as manufacturing complexity increases.

That’s where calibrated virtual twins and machine-learning optimization can help.

**Fig. 1: Systemic failures are a key bottleneck during yield ramp. Faster identification and reduction of these failures can accelerate the yield ramp and shorten the time required to reach a targeted manufacturing yield.**

Process engineers use virtual manufacturing models ([SEMulator3D](https://www.lamresearch.com/product/semulator3d/)) with machine learning (ML) optimization ([Fabtex Yield Optimizer](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/fabtex-yield-optimizer-improves-processes-for-high-volume-manufacturing?blog=true)) to predict process failures.

- A virtual twin can improve DRAM yield analysis by reproducing process variation in a calibrated digital environment.
- ML can then evaluate multiple failure mechanisms and process changes simultaneously.

Using this technique, engineers can evaluate potential yield improvements, all with limited need for wafer-based experimentation.

## Detecting multiple DRAM failure modes with virtual metrology

As an example of this technique, we built a SEMulator3D model (virtual twin) of a DRAM manufacturing process sequence.  During this model-building, we established virtual metrology measurements throughout the process sequence (Figure 2).

**Fig. 2: Building and calibrating a DRAM virtual twin using process integration, virtual metrology, and silicon data.**

ML was then used to calibrate the model against silicon data, enabling the virtual environment to better reproduce observed manufacturing behavior and serve as the foundation for downstream failure analysis and optimization.

## Building and calibrating a DRAM virtual twin

For our specific case study, we built a calibrated virtual twin for our DRAM memory device that contained eight known systemic failure mechanisms.

Figure 3 displays examples of these failure mechanisms, including shorts, opens, and overlap-related defects between critical DRAM structures.

**Fig. 3: Reproducing systemic DRAM failure modes and detecting them using virtual metrology.**

We also specified (in the virtual twin) the virtual metrology needed to detect these failures. By translating each failure into a measurable geometric condition and monitoring it through virtual metrology, we were able to automatically detect and simultaneously analyze multiple failure mechanisms within a single study.

## Using machine learning to optimize process targets

Using the calibrated virtual twin, ML was then applied to help us understand the impact of process and structural variations on the eight predefined failure modes.

We then searched for an optimized manufacturing solution (specific process changes) that provided the lowest failure rate across our eight predefined failure modes. Instead of addressing each failure mode independently, the optimization routine evaluated the impact of multiple process changes simultaneously and searched for process targets that improved the overall pass ratio.

## Case study results: Predicted yield increased to 78.5%

As shown in Figure 4, the optimized process settings significantly reduced all eight systemic failure modes.

**Fig. 4: Simultaneous reduction of multiple systemic failures through ML-based optimization and retargeting analysis. A sample retargeting plot for SNLP (storage node landing pad) open/short failures is highlighted.**

Under the nominal process conditions used in the study, the predicted total yield was 0.1%. Following optimization, the predicted yield increased to 78.5%, with lower failure rates across all eight failure mechanisms.

This analysis also translated the optimized solution into actionable inline fab targets that can be directly applied in the real process, helping engineers identify which process and structural parameters should be adjusted to further reduce systemic failures.

## Accelerating semiconductor yield improvement

This work demonstrates how the combination of process models and ML can be used to accelerate yield improvement during DRAM device development. By reproducing process variability in a calibrated virtual environment, and performing simultaneous optimization and retargeting, engineers can detect multiple device failures and investigate a broad solution space without the time and cost of extensive silicon experimentation.

### Reference

1 I. Tirkel, “Yield Learning Curve Models in Semiconductor Manufacturing,” IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing, vol. 26, no. 4, pp. 564-571, Nov. 2013.

### Related information

- [SEMulator3D – Lam Research](https://www.lamresearch.com/product/semulator3d/)
- [Accelerating GAA Logic Yield Optimization with Digital Twins](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/accelerating-gaa-logic-yield-optimization-with-digital-twins)
- [Unraveling DRAM SAQP Process Complexity with Monte Carlo Virtual Fabrication](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/unraveling-dram-saqp-process-complexity-with-monte-carlo-virtual-fabrication)

items.title: From Metrology To Autonomy: Scaling Yield, Quality, And Innovation
items.content:
With the growth of increasingly complex devices, improving yield, quality, and manufacturing speed requires a new approach. Across 14 presentations and posters presented at SEMICON West 2026, Intel Foundry leaders and engineers shared research and emerging solutions for the AI-ready foundry of the future. By combining end-to-end metrology, intelligent analytics, and industry-wide standards, we can unlock scalable innovation for our customers.

Semiconductor manufacturing is shifting from isolated optimization to connected intelligence, according to Intel Foundry’s Lalitha Immaneni, vice president of semiconductor research and development, advanced packaging technology and manufacturing (APTM), in her keynote at the conference. Factory autonomy will not emerge from AI alone. It requires a system-first mindset based on a common foundation of trusted measurements, interoperable platforms, and advanced test infrastructure.¹

## End-to-end metrology for proactive yield management

For decades, metrology has served as a critical manufacturing checkpoint. Today, it is evolving into a control layer for proactive yield management. Modern semiconductor manufacturing demands more advanced metrology and defect control to address rising contamination risks, process sensitivities, and defectivity challenges. Hidden interactions among materials, equipment, chemicals, packaging polymers, and fab environments can undermine yield and often go undetected until late-stage manufacturing, increasing costs and slowing production. Rather than reacting to failures after they occur, semiconductor manufacturers like Intel Foundry are using predictive process control supported by continuous measurement and monitoring.²

The requirement for end-to-end visibility does not stop at wafer fabrication. The industry’s transition toward heterogeneous integration has introduced increasingly complex architectures built on chiplets, hybrid bonding, high-bandwidth memory, and advanced 2.5D and 3D packaging technologies. These innovations are blurring the traditional boundaries between front-end manufacturing and back-end assembly. Today’s advanced packaging environments require the same level of process intelligence found in leading-edge wafer fabs, such as nanometer-scale precision, process control discipline, and quality assurance capabilities.³

Test operations increasingly represent the final extension of this measurement strategy. Intel Foundry’s Advanced Chiplet Test services provide wafer-to-system test coverage designed to identify issues early, enable known-good die selection, and optimize back-end yield before expensive assembly operations begin. Through predictive die classification, intelligent die pairing, integrated optical testing, and closed-loop yield analytics, test data becomes a critical input for manufacturing intelligence.

## AI-powered insights for yield improvement

Our work on automatic defect classification (ADC) illustrates how AI can help accelerate yield learning and turn complexity into productivity. Managing thousands of classification recipes across multiple technology nodes and manufacturing sites is increasingly difficult, so engineers developed a human-in-the-loop agentic workflow to assist with log analysis, knowledge retrieval, root cause investigation, and recipe reviews. AI-generated recommendations, combined with human approval checkpoints, speed investigations while maintaining auditability and engineering oversight.⁴

We’re also exploring new approaches to thermal intelligence. Our research combines AI with heat-transfer physics to predict how heat moves through semiconductor devices more accurately and with less training data.⁵ This research complements Intel Foundry’s broader investments in advanced test and reliability methodologies, including system-level testing, burn-in, and precision thermal control for increasingly power-dense AI and heterogeneous computing devices. Together, these capabilities help engineers identify yield limiters earlier, reduce manufacturing variability, and make faster, more reliable decisions across the production flow.

## Building an AI-ready manufacturing infrastructure and ecosystem

Precision measurements and intelligent analytics are key components, but scaling in high volume manufacturing requires a modern digital infrastructure. Traditional vendor-locked automation systems often create data silos that limit operational visibility and slow decision-making. By adopting hardware-independent automation architectures, connected data systems, and AI-enabled edge computing, manufacturers can reduce engineering cycles, lower operating costs, and enable predictive maintenance and AI-driven quality inspection.⁶

Finally, autonomy cannot be achieved by technology innovation alone. Industry standards will play a pivotal role. The Semiconductor Assembly Test Automation and Standardization Research Association (SATAS) consortium brings together more than 40 organizations to develop open standards, interoperable architectures, and automation frameworks that can be adopted across the global semiconductor industry, helping to move semiconductor manufacturing from highly automated operations toward true factory autonomy.

SATAS is a multi-year industry initiative sponsored by Japan’s New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) and the Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry (METI). Intel Foundry is helping advance interoperable architectures, automation frameworks, material-handling standards, and collaborative pilot environments that can accelerate back-end manufacturing transformation. By enabling a more connected and interoperable semiconductor ecosystem, Intel Foundry is making it easier for customers and partners to integrate processes, automate workflows, and adopt next-generation manufacturing capabilities.⁷

## A roadmap for the next generation of manufacturing

Operationalizing intelligence across the manufacturing stack is getting closer to reality. It begins with end-to-end metrology and trusted data. It extends through explainable, physics-informed AI and advanced failure analysis methodologies. It relies on resilient automation, edge computing, and advanced packaging platforms. And it scales through ecosystem-wide standards and interoperability. Together, these capabilities help customers lead in the next era of manufacturing.

### Endnotes

The following presentations and posters were presented at SEMICON West in October 2026:

1. Immaneni, L., “The System Era: Scaling AI Through Heterogeneous Integration.”
2. Sengupta, A., “The Importance of End-to-End Advanced Metrology and Defect Control.”
3. Yathapu, N., “Convergence of Advanced Packaging and Front-End Metrology Requirements.”
4. Gemici, M. et al., “Agentic AI Workflow for Automatic Defect Classification Operations in Semiconductor Manufacturing.”
5. Eyde, Z. S., “Preventing Thermal-Related Issues at Final Test Using Physics-Informed Neural Network.”
6. March, S. et al., “Software-Defined Automation: A Blueprint for AI-Ready Edge Computing in Fabs and Facilities.”
7. Haddadin, M., “SATAS: Building the Ecosystem for the Next Generation of Semiconductor Assembly and Test Manufacturing.”

The post [From Metrology To Autonomy: Scaling Yield, Quality, And Innovation](https://semiengineering.com/from-metrology-to-autonomy-scaling-yield-quality-and-innovation/) appeared first on [Semiconductor Engineering](https://semiengineering.com).

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.content:
One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). The findings align with research showing adolescent girls endure very high rates of intimate partner violence.

“These are really sad figures,” said Jean-Paul Murunga, a lawyer with the global human rights organisation Equality Now. “Especially given that the continent of Africa as a whole has adopted the Maputo protocol, which sets \[binding legal standards for\] equality between women and men. We still have a lot of work to do to ensure women and girls benefit from these commitments.”

The Maputo protocol, a landmark treaty adopted by the African Union in 2003, guarantees women’s rights and obliges states to protect women from violence. It affirms that marriage must be based on full consent and guarantees women’s right to health.

“The underlying principle is unambiguous: sexual intercourse without free and voluntary consent constitutes sexual violence, including within marriage,” said Murunga. “Marriage does not create perpetual or implied consent. A woman retains the right to decide whether, when and how she engages in sexual activity”.

He said that as a first step rape laws across the continent needed to change. According to Murunga’s 2024 report, rape within marriage is not criminalised in some African countries. Seven countries expressly exempt husbands from prosecution for marital rape, including Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia and South Sudan. Some countries, such as Tanzania and Eritrea, only criminalise marital rape when the couple do not live together.

In countries where child marriage is permitted and marital rape is not criminalised, children are left unprotected. A legal loophole is created for what, outside marriage, would be classed as rape, and young wives have few options when it comes to protecting themselves from sexual violence and exploitation. In Gabon, for example, when a man has married a child he abducted, he can only be prosecuted after the marriage is annulled.

Underpinning these laws is the mistaken belief that marital rape does not exist as a concept because, by marrying, wives are assumed to have permanently consented to sex with their husbands. In many areas, religion plays a key role in affirming these beliefs.

Alimatu Dimonekene, founder of A Girl At A Time, an organisation supporting adolescent girls in Sierra Leone, said a conversation around consent in marriage had yet to begin in Africa. “We’ve not even started the conversation \[around marital rape\],” she said. “Women will never call it rape; they make excuses for it or even blame themselves.”

She added: “In west Africa, sex is seen as an obligation in marriage. You must do whatever your husband demands.

“Once he has paid your bride price \[a traditional marriage custom in which the bride’s family are paid money, livestock or goods by the groom\], he owns you and you cannot reject his demands. Whatever he wants, he gets, including in terms of intimacy, finances and raising the children.”

items.title: Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Is My Top Memory Stock for 2027. - Yahoo Finance
items.content:
# Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Is My Top Memory Stock for 2027.

**Micron Technology** and **Sandisk** have sizzled on the stock market in 2026. Both stocks have delivered impressive gains this year, despite witnessing a significant pullback in recent months amid the broader correction in tech stocks.

Micron stock, for instance, has gained 128% in 2026, as of this writing. Sandisk's gains are even bigger at 194%. Importantly, both memory companies can step on the gas once again in 2027, driven by the artificial intelligence (AI)-fueled demand for compute and storage.

*Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout.* <u>Continue »</u>

However, I think that Micron and Sandisk could be overshadowed by South Korean memory giant **SK Hynix** (NASDAQ:SKHY) next year. Let's look at the reasons why.

Image source: Getty Images.

## SK Hynix's strong market share puts it in a solid position to capitalize on the memory market's growth

SK Hynix sells both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash memory. Counterpoint Research points out that the company controlled 29% of the DRAM market in the third quarter of 2026. It is second only to **Samsung** in this market. Micron, for comparison, has a 21% share of the DRAM market.

Meanwhile, SK Hynix's 19% share of NAND flash puts it ahead of both Micron and Sandisk, which have market shares of 15% and 11%, respectively. The South Korean company's healthy market shares in both DRAM and NAND flash explain why it reported phenomenal growth in Q3. SK Hynix's revenue surged 328% year over year to $79 billion, easily beating the consensus estimate.

The company's operating profit jumped 632% from the year-ago period and exceeded analysts' expectations. SK Hynix is well-placed to sustain such impressive growth. That's because the company has already sold more than half of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028 under long-term agreements with 14 customers.

Moreover, SK Hynix anticipates that memory demand will outstrip supply through 2030, indicating that the favorable environment fueling the company's stunning growth is sustainable. Also, SK Hynix is ramping up production of its next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, known as HBM4.

It points out that HBM4 has twice the bandwidth of the previous-generation HBM3E chips and 40% higher power efficiency. SK Hynix notes that HBM4 revenue and shipments will surpass those of HBM3E in the current quarter, which should bode well for the company's margins. That's because HBM4 reportedly carries a 24% premium per gigabyte (GB) over the previous generation, HBM3E.

items.title: Bull Shows Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids Package at SC26
items.content:
Intel is doing a mini launch of its next-generation server CPU (or something thereabouts at SC26). There are many systems on the floor, but one, the Bull Sequana XH31600, actually showed Diamond Rapids packages.

## Bull Shows Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids Package at SC26

Starting off, here is the Bull compute blade with blind mate power and liquid at the rear, networking in front, and four Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids packages up front.

Just ot be clear about what you are seeing, these are two dual-socket compute nodes with Intel Diamond Rapids, each with 16-channel memory.

Here is a view of the package. We have already seen the LGA9324 socket covered in the ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ from OCP Summit 2026.

You can see that in the Bull platform, the CPUs are on fairly wide motherboards because of all of the memory on either side.

The idea is that these blades are liquid cooled, so you can see how everything has heatpipes and liquid cooling blocks.

The other node had the liquid cooling blocks as well as the cabled connections to the networking.

On the networking, Bull had its BXI technology for interconnect. In its booth, Bull showed a BXI switch with 64x 800G OSFP ports, but the BXI NICs were shown as QSFP-DD and PCIe Gen5 x16. It actually looks like Bull is doing something similar to what we did with the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 C8240 800G Dual 400G NIC Review This is a SuperNIC when we managed to use two PCIe Gen5 x16 links to get 800Gbps from the ConnectX-8.

What stood out a bit is that there was an NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC as well in an OCP NIC 3.0 form factor. It’s interesting that Bull has its own interconnect, with a 51.2T switch and a PCIe Gen5 NIC in a platform with a Gen6 CPU, but right next to it is NVIDIA’s high-volume PCIe Gen6 NIC competitor.

What is very cool about this platform is that it is incredibly bespoke.

For years, Bull has had one of the better-looking blade designs, largely because they liquid-cool everything. Probably worth pondering, however, is that with NVIDIA pushing the industry with ORv3, and AMD now with the double-wide. It feels like there is a high-volume standard for high-density racks in the industry if you want power and cooling. Maybe the more interesting part is that Bull’s design does not have a copper-cabled backplane in the rear.

Overall, this was very neat to see.

## Final Words

What has been interesting at SC26 is that this type of platform would have been mind-blowing years ago. Now, with the NVIDIA Vera Rubin designs in ORv3 racks, the Bull systems fit in with the higher-volume AI infrastructure bits. What Bull has, however, is SiPearl, Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids, NVIDIA, and AMD Venice nodes on display in a common form factor.

Many other vendors are showing off Diamond Rapids systems with neat designs, including 32DIMM/ socket 2DPC configurations at SC26. For its part, Bull is the only one we have found that has a package. Diamond Rapids seems to be in the sampling phase. The best guess is maybe we start to see a launch in Q2 2027, but if that slips past June (or it becomes a split launch with 1P platforms and 2P platforms), the next real launch window for Intel is early September 2027.

items.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
items.content:
Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.

It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. However, judges at the court have taken advice on how to protect their assets from potential US sanctions, as a genocide ruling could be interpreted by Washington as lowering the “legal threshold” for the crime.

The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.

The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.

The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.

The US has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The US has also announced sanctions against the entire ICC as an institution, which it described as a “rogue court”. Washington fears the ICC could go after US troops.

The Gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against Myanmar and chose the South African lawyer Pillay, who in October was awarded the Nobel peace prize. She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.

Waltz asserted last month: “The ICJ ad hoc judge Navi Pillay is tipping the scales on the ICJ’s current proceedings on Myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against American and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians.”

In remarks addressed to Pillay, he said: “We see your agenda and we’ll be watching the ICJ’s handling of these proceedings very closely.”

In a speech last Friday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said: “For this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles.”

after newsletter promotion

He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.

Israel has previously criticised adverse advisory opinions issued by the ICJ and refused to implement 2024 orders requiring Israel to admit more aid into Gaza, and to cooperate with Unrwa, the UN relief and works agency.

In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.

It also stressed that genocide was not solely defined by killings, and that the treatment of children, gender-based violence and forced displacement were also relevant.

The US until recently had taken a relatively more benign view of The Hague-based ICJ, and under Antony Blinken as US secretary of state determined that Myanmar had committed genocide.

The 15 ICJ judges are elected for nine-year terms by the UN security council and the UN general assembly.

Rubio has given the ICC until April to respond to his criticisms before he imposes sanctions.

On Friday, the ICC formally decided to drop plans to prosecute US soldiers and intelligence agents for potentially unlawful acts in Afghanistan. The shelving of the near-dormant inquiry came after it was agreed evidence would be hard to obtain, but one side-effect may be a greater willingness on the part of the US to abandon its plan to impose sanctions on the ICC.

items.title: 黄仁勋归期悬而未决，买GPU的人已经不敢下单
items.content:
“现在都不敢订期货。”在深圳负责GPU采购的程麟，用一句话概括了今年的处境。

从突然辞任，到传出回归，再到本人公开表达重返意愿、董事会却在财报电话会上明确表示无意让其复职——短短五天里，围绕黄仁勋去留的消息几度反转。

多方信源此前也向雷峰网表示，黄仁勋短期内很难重新执掌英伟达。

但对于依赖英伟达GPU开展生意的中国算力服务商而言，眼下更现实的问题是：即便黄仁勋回来了，高端GPU还能不能买到？买到后又该如何变现？

国内买英伟达GPU的渠道在收窄，海外租算力也不轻松。程麟所在团队曾尝试通过自建、投资海外机房等方式获取算力资源，但机房建设周期长达两三年。随着美国对先进GPU流转的监管趋严，部分在建项目已开始重新评估。

而他考虑的另一条路——华为昇腾950，据其了解当前订单排期已经排满，交付周期同样存在不确定性。

**01**

#### **黄仁勋想做中国生意**

#### **美国却在收紧每一条路**

“做生意能够赚钱，（黄仁勋）为什么不争取美国政府放松管控？”算力服务商Jason Lee直言。

但如今，黄仁勋的商业诉求，正与美国不断收紧的对华芯片管制发生正面碰撞。

自去年以来，美国国会议员先后推动四项针对先进芯片出口及流转的法案，分别涉及出口审批、芯片位置核验、盟友半导体制造设备出口管制，以及通过云服务等方式远程访问受控芯片等产品的行为监管。

目前，国会两党部分议员正推动将上述法案纳入2027财年《国防授权法案》（NDAA）的最终文本。按照当前进度，NDAA最早可能于今年12月进入院会表决阶段。

美国对先进AI芯片的监管正向设备出口后的流转环节延伸，这也是Jason判断黄仁勋离任影响有限的原因。

“无论黄仁勋是否继续担任CEO，都不会改变美国收紧对华GPU供应的方向。”Jason指出，这反映了美国对中国AI能力的担忧，背后牵扯出中美之间的科技竞争。

芯片行业分析师小杜直言，恐怕连黄仁勋本人也没有充分预料到，AI在这几年发展得如此迅速，逐渐从普通产业技术上升为与国家安全密切相关的战略能力。

不少受访者认为风险迟早会来，只是没想到黄仁勋会成为第一个被“开刀”的对象。

在小杜看来，相比英伟达，其他芯片企业原本也有动力争取中国市场，但在对华业务上表现得相对谨慎。而在黄仁勋主导下的英伟达却更加激进，甚至有些“揣着明白装糊涂”。

小杜补充：“虽然国内有不少企业参与高端GPU供卡业务，但真正掌握核心渠道和资源的团队其实就那么几个人。”这意味着如果美国有意追查，很容易就能顺藤摸瓜，查清相关利益链条。

因此黄仁勋过去在中国市场的冒进打法是否会引来进一步追责，最终还要看美国政府愿意将监管推进到哪一步。

大势之下，英伟达自身的合规管理也明显加码。

一方面，早在黄仁勋辞任前，外媒已曝出英伟达已经开始要求东南亚部分希望获得其云合作伙伴资格的客户，接入能够收集AI加速器部署位置等信息的Fleet Intelligence系统。

另一方面，日前英伟达首次在董事会下设立专门委员会，聚焦监督国家安全与芯片出口管制事务。

**02**

#### **一台B300炒至2200万 灰色通道里的暴利与违约**

政策层面的变化，早已引起部分算力服务商的警觉。

Jason回忆，自己从今年上半年就开始对东南亚的GPU转运渠道保持谨慎。面对一些声称能够通过马来西亚将GPU运进国内的渠道商，他的态度很明确：先把设备真正运进来，再谈后续合作。

之后马来西亚渐渐传出GPU服务器被海关查扣的消息，让他更加确定这类交易的风险。在Jason看来，美国对第三国设备流转的监管正在加强，过去一些看似可行的转运渠道，已经很难继续依赖。

但即便跨境交易的风险越来越高，仍有人愿意铤而走险。“赔钱的生意没人做，‘杀头’的生意总有人敢做。”某AI芯片企业高管对此评价道。

从事算力服务生意已有两年的晓宇给雷峰网算了一笔账：B300出厂价格约为400万元，海外实际采购成本达到700万至800万元，一旦运转至国内，市场报价立马翻倍。

巨大的价差从何而来？首先，海外机房**GPU订货额度本身就有交易价值**。

晓宇向雷峰网解释，海外数据中心采购高性能GPU，通常需要向上游供应商提交企业背景、机房条件及最终用途等资料，等待KYC（Know Your Customer，了解你的客户）审查。

而审核通过只是前提。晓宇补充，机房能够承接的GPU订货数量，还取决于**自身电力容量**等基础设施条件。

在此基础上，由于美国直接限制先进GPU对华出口并严查流向，货源进入灰色渠道后，高昂的合规风险还将转化为溢价。

Jason透露，在黄仁勋风波前，国内单台B300现货价已攀升至2200万元左右。

从设备本身到采购渠道，再到正式入境，层层加价在推高GPU市场报价的同时，也让晓宇这类采购方吃了一次亏。

此前，他所在团队计划从海外采购数十台B300，甚至提前买好了交换机、网卡等配套设备，最终供应方却只交付了两台。

晓宇认为，问题恰恰出在违约成本太低。随着市场报价不断上涨，供应商即使放弃原有订单，需要支付的违约金也可能远低于重新出售设备获得的收益。

**03**

#### **转战海外卖算力 卡在1200万算力红线与机房运维**

面对高端GPU设备跨境难度和违约风险的增加，晓宇所在团队眼下也更注重发展另一种商业模式——将GPU留在海外数据中心，通过算力租赁、Token计费等形式服务当地和国内客户。

然而，将GPU留在海外，算力也未必好卖。

晓宇解释，马来西亚、泰国等地的本地AI生态和算力需求相对有限，部分机房的算力规模已经超过当地市场的消化能力，这意味着国内客户仍在主导需求市场。

但这条路和“把设备运进国内”一样不轻松，海外算力服务的最终客户和用途同样进入美国监管视野。

此前有外媒报道称，美国计划将马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚、挪威、巴西和南非等七国纳入先进AI芯片出口许可管理。

日前，美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）公布的新规最终列出五国，挪威、南非未被纳入。

除了缩水的名单外，新规还为远程算力设定了一道规模门槛：若海外数据中心向总部或最终母公司总部位于受限范围的企业提供超过1200万TPP（总计算能力）的算力，相关先进芯片的出口、再出口及境内转移均需申请许可。

该受限范围当前涵盖美国《出口管理条例》（EAR）D:5组（含中国大陆及中国香港）和中国澳门。不过，即便直接客户未被列入此范围，只要算力最终流向受限企业，同样可能触发许可要求。

而1200万TPP究竟意味着多大规模的算力？按照BIS的TPP计算规则估算，**约相当于95台8卡H200 SXM服务器（FP8）或27台8卡B300服务器（FP4）**。

在合规用途的机器越来越难拿的背景下，要让几十台乃至上百台高端服务器稳定运转，机房本身的建设与运营同样不易。

晓宇举例，过去东南亚出现过一些与国内企业合作搭建的方舱式机房，部分项目主要围绕GPU倒货展开，实际可用性有限。

这类机房如果想继续经营，需要具备稳定的电力供应、专业的运维能力，以及持续对外提供算力服务的能力，才能真正把机器运行起来。

**04**

#### **缺卡的市场 国产GPU未必有份**

美国收紧英伟达高端GPU对华供应，理论上为国产GPU腾出了市场空间，但眼下的利好预期更多反映在股价上，产业端的信心仍未同步提升。

国产GPU能否接住市场需求，还要看具体的应用场景。

训练端仍难撬动。多位受访者表示，即使英伟达GPU因供应受限而价格上涨，对于大厂和模型公司而言，只要能够支撑前沿模型训练，它们还是愿意溢价支付。

相较之下，国产GPU更容易争取的推理市场又未必算得过账。

有受访者观察到，从H系列开始，英伟达显卡虽然单价较高，但如果按最终推理产出计算，单位成本反而可能低于部分价格更便宜的国产卡。

行业分析师秦擎解释，推理业务的盈利空间高度依赖Token售价和生产这些token所需要承担的计算成本。如果国产卡无法在HBM成本和计算效率上形成优势，即使单卡采购价格较低，商业化仍然面临压力。

据秦擎了解，由于国内企业很难直接与国外原厂签约，国内一些HBM的采购成本至少达到海外正常采购价格的两倍。

与此同时，国内HBM供应也在等待新的产能释放。但小杜调研后认为，长鑫的产能起码要到明年才可能成为新的变量。

压力不止于此，逻辑芯片的制造与先进封装产能，同样困扰着国产GPU厂商。

小杜指出，芯片设计公司理论上应该凭借架构、软件和设计能力获得更高溢价，但各家国产芯片厂商在将这些能力转化为市场竞争优势之前，就已经先被制造产能和HBM供应卡住，呈现“**供应链的溢价比设计能力更高**”的局面。

供应链的协同运转，仍将是国产GPU厂商未来一年绕不开的集体大考。

\* 文中受访者均为匿名。
